name: STM32F205RBT6
title: STM32F205xx/STM32F207xx: 120 MHz Cortex-M3 microcontrollers, up to 1 MB flash, 128 KB + 4 KB SRAM, USB OTG HS/FS, Ethernet (F207), 1.8 V to 3.6 V
summary: A family of 32-bit Arm Cortex-M3 microcontrollers that run at up to 120 MHz from a 1.8 V to 3.6 V supply, with an ART flash accelerator that gives zero-wait-state performance from the 128-bit-wide flash. Parts carry 128 KB to 1 MB of flash, 64 KB to 128 KB of system SRAM plus 4 KB of battery-backed SRAM, three 12-bit 2 Msps ADCs, two 12-bit DACs, up to 17 timers, USB OTG full-speed and high-speed (ULPI) controllers, two CAN, SDIO, up to six U(S)ARTs, three SPI/two I2S and three I2C; the STM32F207xx adds a 10/100 Ethernet MAC and a camera interface. Packages run from LQFP64 and WLCSP64+2 to LQFP176 and UFBGA176. The STM32F205RBT6 is the LQFP64 part with 128 KB of flash, 64 KB + 4 KB of SRAM and 51 I/Os, for -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M3, 120 MHz max, MPU, 150 DMIPS (1.25 DMIPS/MHz, Dhrystone 2.1)
64, 96 or 128 KB system SRAM + 4 KB backup SRAM; RBT6: 64 KB (48 + 16) + 4 KB
VDD 1.8 V to 3.6 V (1.7 V on WLCSP64+2 with IRROFF high, 0 °C to 70 °C); VBAT 1.65 V to 3.6 V
49 mA typ at 120 MHz from RAM or flash with ART on, all peripherals on (VDD = 3.3 V, 25 °C)
Stop 0.30 mA to 0.55 mA typ; Standby 1.7 µA to 3.0 µA typ at VDD = 1.8 V; VBAT 0.10 µA to 1.29 µA typ
3 × 12-bit ADC, up to 2 Msps each, 6 Msps triple interleaved, up to 24 channels; 2 × 12-bit DAC
HSE 4 MHz to 26 MHz crystal, HSI 16 MHz RC (±1% at 25 °C), LSE 32.768 kHz, LSI 32 kHz, main PLL and audio PLL
USB OTG FS with PHY, USB OTG HS (ULPI), 2 × CAN 2.0B, SDIO, 4 USART + 2 UART, 3 SPI (2 with I2S), 3 I2C; Ethernet MAC and camera interface on STM32F207xx
51 to 140 I/Os, up to 138 of them 5 V tolerant; RBT6: 51
LQFP64, WLCSP64+2, LQFP100, LQFP144, LQFP176, UFBGA176

notes: Every part: Cortex-M3 at up to 120 MHz, 1.8 V to 3.6 V, 10 general-purpose, 2 advanced-control and 2 basic timers, IWDG, WWDG, RTC, random number generator, 3 SPI (2 with I2S), 3 I2C, 4 USART, 2 UART, USB OTG FS, USB OTG HS, 2 CAN, SDIO, three 12-bit ADCs and a 2-channel 12-bit DAC.
(1) On LQFP100 only FSMC Bank1 (multiplexed NOR/PSRAM on NE1) and Bank2 (8- or 16-bit NAND on NCE2) are usable, and the NAND interrupt line is absent because Port G is not bonded out.
SPI2 and SPI3 each work either as SPI or as I2S, not both at once.

The order code adds package, temperature and option letters to the part number: T = LQFP, H = UFBGA, Y = WLCSP; 6 = -40 °C to 85 °C, 7 = -40 °C to 105 °C (see the ordering scheme). STM32F205RBT6: LQFP64, -40 °C to 85 °C.
Junction temperature range of the family: -40 °C to 125 °C.

operation.text: Two lines share pins, software and features. The STM32F205xx has everything except Ethernet and the camera interface; the STM32F207xx has both. Memory size, package and I/O count set the rest. The FSMC exists only in packages of 100 pins or more.

Functional pins match the STM32F10xx, but the power pins differ, so a board for both needs a few options: on LQFP64 a 0 Ω link or solder bridge to VSS is fitted for the F10x and left open for the F2; on LQFP100 and LQFP144 two more 0 Ω links go to VSS for the F10x and to VDD, VSS or nothing for the F2, and the F2's RFU pin sits where the F10x has a VSS.

The Cortex-M3 runs at up to 120 MHz. The ART accelerator puts an instruction prefetch queue and a branch cache in front of the 128-bit flash, so code from flash runs as fast as with no wait states at full speed (measured with CoreMark).
Up to 8 protected regions, each split into 8 subregions, from 32 bytes up to the full 4 GB; an access the MPU forbids can be caught by an RTOS. It can be left unused.

Flash of 128 KB to 1 MB on a 128-bit bus; 512 bytes of OTP for data such as MAC addresses or keys; up to 128 KB of system SRAM read and written at CPU speed with no wait states; 4 KB of backup SRAM, guarded against stray writes and kept in Standby and VBAT modes. A 32-bit multi-AHB matrix links the CPU, both DMAs, the Ethernet MAC and USB HS to the flash, SRAMs, FSMC and peripherals.
Computes a CRC on 32-bit words with a fixed polynomial, for example to check flash contents at run time against a value stored at link time (EN/IEC 60335-1).

Two dual-port DMA controllers with 8 streams each handle memory-to-memory and peripheral transfers with shared FIFOs, bursts, circular buffers and double buffering. Each stream has its own hardware requests and a software trigger. They serve SPI/I2S, I2C, U(S)ART, timers, DAC, SDIO, DCMI and ADC.

Four chip selects for PC Card/CompactFlash, SRAM, PSRAM, NOR and NAND, with a write FIFO; code can execute from external memory except NAND and PC Card; external accesses run with fHCLK up to 60 MHz. It also drives graphic LCD controllers in Intel 8080 or Motorola 6800 mode.

The NVIC handles 81 maskable channels plus the 16 Cortex-M3 lines at 16 priority levels, with tail chaining and late-arrival handling. The EXTI has 23 edge detectors, each set to rising, falling or both edges and masked on its own; up to 140 GPIOs map onto its 16 external lines and it catches pulses shorter than an APB2 clock period.

After reset the CPU runs from the 16 MHz HSI RC (factory trimmed to 1%). Software can switch to a 4 MHz to 26 MHz external clock, which is watched: on failure the system falls back to the HSI and can raise an interrupt. PLLs and prescalers set the three AHB buses (120 MHz max), APB2 (60 MHz max) and APB1 (30 MHz max). A separate audio PLL (PLLI2S) gives I2S sample rates from 8 kHz to 192 kHz. USB OTG needs a 48 MHz clock from the PLL on the HSE.

The boot pins select user flash, system memory or embedded SRAM. The boot loader in system memory reprograms flash over USART1 (PA9/PA10), USART3 (PC10/PC11 or PB10/PB11), CAN2 (PB5/PB13) or USB OTG FS in device mode (PA11/PA12) using DFU.

VDD (1.8 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os and the regulator. VDDA and VSSA (1.8 V to 3.6 V) feed the ADC, DAC, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL, and are connected to VDD and VSS. VBAT (1.65 V to 3.6 V) keeps the RTC, LSE and backup registers alive through a power switch when VDD is gone. On WLCSP64+2 with IRROFF at VDD and an external supervisor, VDD may go down to 1.7 V between 0 °C and 70 °C.

POR and PDR are always on and hold the chip in reset below the VPOR/PDR or VBOR threshold with no external circuit. Once the POR level is passed the option bytes load, which keep or change the BOR level (three thresholds) or turn BOR off. The PVD compares VDD/VDDA with a programmable level and can interrupt on falling below or rising above it; software enables it. On WLCSP64+2, IRROFF at VDD turns POR, PDR and BOR off and an external supervisor takes over.

The default on LQFP packages; on WLCSP64+2 with REGOFF and IRROFF at VSS, on UFBGA176 with REGOFF at VSS. Minimum VDD is 1.8 V. The main regulator runs in normal operation, the low-power regulator in Stop mode, and in Standby the regulator is powered down (output high impedance, register and SRAM contents lost). VCAP_1 and VCAP_2 each need a 2.2 µF ceramic with ESR under 2 Ω.

Only on packages with a REGOFF pin: REGOFF high turns the regulator off and a 1.2 V supply (1.1 V to 1.3 V) goes in on VCAP_1 and VCAP_2, whose 2.2 µF capacitors become 100 nF. Nothing inside then watches the 1.2 V rail, so an external supervisor drives PA0 as the power-on reset of the 1.2 V domain; PA0 is then not a GPIO, and while it is low the debugger cannot connect at power-on reset, so PA0 and NRST are handled separately when debug at reset is wanted. VDD stays above VCAP_1/VCAP_2. With internal reset still on (WLCSP64+2 IRROFF at VSS, or UFBGA176), VDD/VDDA minimum is 1.8 V. With internal reset off (WLCSP64+2 only, REGOFF at VSS and IRROFF at VDD), POR, PDR, BOR, PVD and VBAT are all disabled and the supervisor keeps the chip in reset below 1.8 V on VDD (1.7 V between 0 °C and 70 °C) and 1.08 V on VCAP.

With a slow VDD ramp, PA0 tied to NRST holds reset until both VDD has passed the 1.8 V PDR level and VCAP has passed 1.08 V. With a fast VDD ramp, where VDD gets there before VCAP, PA0 is held low from outside until VCAP reaches 1.08 V. The slow-ramp sequence is the same with the internal reset on or off.

The backup domain holds the RTC, 4 KB of backup SRAM and 20 32-bit backup registers (80 bytes), all fed through a switch from VDD or VBAT. The RTC is a BCD calendar (seconds to year, 12/24 h, leap years handled) with two maskable alarms, a 16-bit auto-reload wakeup timer covering 120 µs to 36 hours, a 20-bit prescaler (1 s from 32.768 kHz by default), a 512 Hz calibration output and a 50/60 Hz reference input. It runs from the LSE crystal, the LSI RC (32 kHz typ) or HSE/128, and can wake the chip from Stop and Standby. The backup SRAM is off by default to save power. Backup registers survive system and power resets and Standby wakeup.

Sleep stops only the CPU; any interrupt or event wakes it. Stop halts every clock in the 1.2 V domain and turns off the PLL, HSI and HSE while SRAM and registers keep their contents; the regulator runs in normal or low-power mode; any EXTI line wakes it (external lines, PVD, RTC alarm/wakeup/tamper/time stamp, USB OTG FS/HS wakeup, Ethernet wakeup). Standby powers off the whole 1.2 V domain and loses SRAM and registers except the backup domain and backup SRAM; NRST, IWDG reset, a rising edge on WKUP or an RTC event wakes it. The RTC, IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.

When VDD is absent, VBAT supplies the RTC, backup registers and backup SRAM. External interrupts and RTC events do not end VBAT operation. On WLCSP64+2 with IRROFF at VDD, VBAT is not available and the pin is tied to VDD.

Two advanced-control timers (TIM1, TIM8) are three-phase PWM generators on 6 channels with complementary outputs and dead time, or full general-purpose timers. TIM2 and TIM5 are 32-bit, TIM3 and TIM4 16-bit, all with 4 channels, quadrature encoder and Hall-sensor inputs and their own DMA requests. TIM9 and TIM12 have 2 channels, TIM10, TIM11, TIM13 and TIM14 one, all 16-bit up-counters. TIM6 and TIM7 are basic time bases that mainly trigger the DAC. Timers can be chained and synchronized, and every counter can freeze in debug.

The independent watchdog is a 12-bit down-counter with an 8-bit prescaler on its own 32 kHz RC, so it keeps running in Stop and Standby; hardware or software start is chosen in the option bytes. The window watchdog is a 7-bit down-counter on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down-counter with a maskable interrupt at zero and a selectable clock.

Up to three I2C interfaces, multimaster or slave, standard and fast mode, 7/10-bit and dual 7-bit slave addressing, hardware CRC, DMA, SMBus 2.0 and PMBus. The SDA and SCL pins are not true open-drain: in open-drain mode the PMOS to VDD is switched off but still there.

USART1, USART2, USART3 and USART6 add RTS/CTS, ISO 7816 smart card and synchronous SPI-like modes to what UART4 and UART5 offer: asynchronous mode, IrDA SIR, multiprocessor mode, single-wire half duplex and LIN master/slave. USART1 and USART6 reach 7.5 Mbit/s, the rest 3.75 Mbit/s. All use DMA.

Three SPIs, master or slave, full duplex or simplex: SPI1 to 30 Mbit/s, SPI2 and SPI3 to 15 Mbit/s, 8 master clock rates from a 3-bit prescaler, 8- or 16-bit frames, hardware CRC for SD/MMC and a TI mode. SPI2 and SPI3 can instead be I2S interfaces: master or slave, half duplex, 16 or 32 bits, 8 kHz to 192 kHz, with a master clock output of 256 × fs. All use DMA.

SD/SDIO/MMC host for MMC 4.2 with 1-, 4- and 8-bit buses up to 48 MHz in 8-bit mode, SD memory card 2.0, SDIO card 2.0 (1- and 4-bit) and CE-ATA 1.1. One SD/SDIO/MMC 4.2 card at a time, or a stack of MMC 4.1 or older.

IEEE 802.3-2002 MAC for 10/100 Mbit/s with an external PHY over MII (17 signals) or RMII (9 signals); the chip can output 25 MHz (MII) or 50 MHz (RMII) to clock the PHY. It has its own DMA, VLAN tags, half and full duplex, control frames, CRC generation and stripping, address filtering, 2 KB transmit and 2 KB receive FIFOs, and hardware IEEE 1588-2008 time stamping tied to TIM2 with a target-time interrupt.
Two CAN 2.0A/B active controllers up to 1 Mbit/s, each with three transmit mailboxes and two 3-stage receive FIFOs, sharing 28 filter banks; each has 256 bytes of its own SRAM.

USB 2.0 full-speed device/host/OTG with on-chip PHY, OTG 1.0, SRP and HNP, 4 bidirectional endpoints, 8 host channels, 320 × 35-bit shared FIFO and no external resistors needed. It runs from a 48 MHz PLL clock. Host and OTG use need an external power switch for bus-powered devices.

USB 2.0 high-speed (480 Mbit/s) device/host/OTG with an internal full-speed PHY and a ULPI port (12 signals, SDR, 60 MHz) for an external high-speed PHY; 6 bidirectional endpoints, 12 host channels, 1024 × 35-bit FIFO, its own DMA, SRP and HNP.

8- to 14-bit parallel input from CMOS sensors, a 27 MHz PIXCLK carries up to 27 Mbyte/s and a 48 MHz clock up to 48 Mbyte/s, with programmable clock and sync polarity, monochrome/raw Bayer, YCbCr 4:2:2, RGB 565 or compressed data, continuous or snapshot capture and cropping.
An analog true random number generator delivering 32-bit values.

Each pin is input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), output, push-pull or open-drain, optionally with a pull resistor, or alternate function, with selectable speed. The configuration can be locked. GPIOs sit on AHB1 at up to 120 MHz and toggle at up to 60 MHz. Outputs sink or source 8 mA, or 20 mA with relaxed levels; PC13 to PC15 and PI8 only 3 mA. The total sourced or sunk by all I/Os plus the run current stays within IVDD and IVSS (120 mA).

Three 12-bit ADCs share up to 16 external channels each (24 on the larger packages), in single or scan mode, with simultaneous or interleaved sample-and-hold, DMA and an analog watchdog. TIM1, TIM2, TIM3, TIM4, TIM5 and TIM8 can trigger regular and injected conversions. Negative current injected into any analog pin badly hurts accuracy of conversions on other pins; positive injection within the IINJ limits does not.

Two buffered 12-bit DAC channels built from resistor strings and an inverting amplifier: 8- or 12-bit monotonic, left or right aligned, synchronized updates, noise and triangle generation, DMA, external triggers through timer update outputs, reference VREF+. The output buffer can be bypassed with BOFFx in DAC_CR.

The temperature sensor is wired to ADC1_IN16 and works over VDD 1.8 V to 3.6 V. Its offset varies from part to part, so it suits measuring changes; an external sensor is needed for absolute temperature. VBAT can be read through an internal 2:1 bridge (50 kΩ), and VREFINT (1.21 V typ) is also measurable.

The SWJ-DP combines JTAG and serial wire debug; JTMS and JTCK double as SWDIO and SWCLK, and a set sequence on TMS switches between the two. The ETM streams compressed instruction and data trace through the TRACECLK and TRACED pins to an external trace port analyzer.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Min and max are guaranteed at worst-case temperature, supply and frequency by production tests at TA = 25 °C and TAmax; values footnoted as characterization or design are not tested, and characterization limits are mean ± 3σ. Typicals are at TA = 25 °C and VDD = 3.3 V; typical ADC accuracy is mean ± 2σ over temperature. Typical curves are guides, not tested.

The supply range limits flash speed, ADC rate, I/O compensation, FSMC clock and flash programming width: from 1.8 V to 2.1 V, 16 MHz without wait states and 7 at 120 MHz, 1 Msps, 8-bit programming; up to 3.6 V above 2.7 V, 30 MHz without wait states, 3 at 120 MHz, 2 Msps, 32-bit programming and a 60 MHz FSMC clock from 3.0 V. The ART accelerator hides the wait states.

A 4 MHz to 26 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator with load capacitors of 5 pF to 25 pF (high-quality, high-frequency ceramics, usually equal). The load capacitance the crystal manufacturer gives is the series value of CL1 and CL2 plus pin and board capacitance (about 10 pF). Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the pins as possible to limit distortion and start-up time. Selection guide: ST application note AN2867.
A 32.768 kHz crystal or resonator with its load capacitors close to OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT. Start-up takes about 2 s and depends strongly on the crystal.

EMC depends heavily on the application and its software. Software should recover from a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers. Most such failures can be provoked for testing by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s, or by ESD applied directly to the part (ST application note AN1015).
The main PLL can spread its output in center-spread or down-spread mode to cut EMI. The modulation period and step are rounded to integers, which quantizes the depth actually reached.

The ULPI clock from the external PHY is 60 MHz ±500 ppm at steady state with a 50% duty cycle, reached within 1.4 ms of the first transition; the clock starts within 5.6 ms after SuspendM is released in peripheral mode.

The junction temperature follows TA max plus PD max times ΘJA, with PD the sum of internal power (IDD × VDD) and output power. ΘJA runs from 38 °C/W (LQFP176) to 51 °C/W (WLCSP64+2); LQFP64 is 45 °C/W.
